### Fixed
- **A `kagent.modelConfigs[]` entry's `provider` is checked against the ModelConfig CRD's enum at render time** (giantswarm/agent-platform#357): `agent-platform.modelConfigProvider` fails the render for any other value, naming the entry and the ten providers — `Anthropic`, `OpenAI`, `AzureOpenAI`, `Ollama`, `Gemini`, `GeminiVertexAI`, `AnthropicVertexAI`, `Bedrock`, `SAPAICore`, `Foundry`, case-sensitive as the CRD's. Until now `provider: openai` rendered and the API server refused the object at apply time with the enum error, after the chart had said nothing. The `baseUrl` already goes under the CRD's block key through `agent-platform.modelConfigBaseUrlKey` (#333: `anthropic`, `openAI`, `sapAICore`, the three `ModelConfigSpec` gives one; the render refuses a `baseUrl` on the seven others), in `templates/kagent/modelconfigs.yaml` and the `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` alike; what was missing was the pin. `ci/test-llm-routing-values.yaml` carries an OpenAI entry with its own `baseUrl`, so `make verify-kagent-crds` validates the `openAI` key against the kagent line's CRD on every run — and now sweeps every provider of the CRD's `spec.provider` enum, read from the CRD at `KAGENT_LINE_REF`: each renders, a `baseUrl` lands under the block the CRD gives one to and nowhere else, the render refuses it where the CRD's block has none, and a provider outside the enum (a lower-cased spelling included) fails naming the enum; a re-pin that moves the enum or a block's fields fails the check naming the helper to move with it. `make verify-llm-routing` asserts the `openAI` key for an explicit URL and for the routed default with `llmRouting.backend.provider: openai`, and the enum guard. Lab-proven on agentlab (Kubernetes 1.37, the line's controller): the fixture's OpenAI ModelConfig applied as rendered, `spec.openAI.baseUrl` survived admission and the kagent controller reported `Accepted` and `ResolvedRefs`; the same object with the lower-cased `openai` block lost the field to pruning with a non-strict client and was `Accepted` all the same (a strict client refuses it as an unknown field) — the silent direct path the issue describes. **No installation acts**: every valid catalog renders byte-identically; only a render that the API server would have refused fails earlier.
